newsitem.title: USA: Smith Barney cuts Peru weighting to neutral.
newsitem.headline: Smith Barney cuts Peru weighting to neutral.

text.p: Smith Barney analyst James Barrineau said Thursday he had cut his recommended weighting on Peru in his Latin American portfolio to neutral from overweight in light of the hsotage crisis in Lima.
"On the heels of the hostage incident, we recommend investors sit tight. This could well be a buying opportunity, but the time is not now," he said in a research note.
"As we write this, the outcome of the hostage situation in Peru is uncertain," he said.
He said the chance of the incident turning out favorably for President Alberto Fujimori "in terms of a dramatic, positive conclusion" was about 20 percent.
"It is more likely to result in lingering damage to investor perceptions of Peru," he said.
But he said he believed Peru's economy could survive a shock to confidence.
He said he had cut his Peru weighting to three percent from four percent.
